notes: hw7 script reads three EPA extracts with three different raw-text layouts (a multi-record @/@@-held layout, a plain CSV, and a wide fixed-count-loop layout), transposes a PM10 dataset, concatenates all four sources, merges in site metadata and measurement-method metadata, applies a custom AQICAT format, does string/date cleanup, and compares the result against an instructor answer key. None of the six source tables, the raw CSVs, or the instructor reference are in the repo (course-proprietary, excluded by .gitignore); the InputDS AQICAT format catalog member is also mocked. autoexec.sas builds small versions of everything, matching columns/informats/delimiters exactly. Two substitutions beyond mock data: (1) PROC TRANSPOSE's VAR range is shrunk from day1-day140/day145-day247/day250-day273/day141-day144 (247 columns, sized for a specific unavailable dataset) to day1-day5 -- same mechanics, fewer of the same-shaped columns; (2) the original's second (descriptor-level) PROC COMPARE is omitted, same as t002, since it depended on the same Jenner ODS OUTPUT POSITION= bug (see below) -- the final PROC CONTENTS itself is kept unmodified. The content-level PROC COMPARE runs against a self-derived reference (a copy of the merged output) since no instructor answer key exists. All DATA/PROC logic, informats, labels and the data-cleaning branch logic (parameter-code lookup, AQI category, percent calculation) are otherwise unmodified from the source. Reuses the same two Jenner engine gaps found while building t002 (both filed as isolated minimal regression tests upstream, internal tracker only, not referenced in the PR): INFILE fileref(member-name) aggregate-storage syntax reading 0 rows, and ODS OUTPUT POSITION=ds from PROC CONTENTS not materializing its target dataset.
